question.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨3t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))^{2}+(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+16{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{9+16({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}5\,\text{d}u \\  & =5u\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =5t\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=5t$, we have that $t=\frac{s}{5}.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{5}) \\  & =⟨3\cdot \frac{s}{5},\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{5}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{s}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3s}{5},\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
